hello.note: Just as common, to anyone: કેમ છો? (kem chho?). Many Gujaratis also greet with જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ (jay shri krushna).

goodbye.note: Literally 'come again'. Both sides say it; the one leaving may also say આવું છું (aavun chhun), 'I'll come again'.

please.note: Formal. In speech, politeness usually comes from the -jo/-sho verb endings, e.g. આપજો (aapjo).

thank_you.note: Also ધન્યવાદ (dhanyavaad). In everyday speech many people simply say 'thank you'.

youre_welcome.note: Gujarati has no set reply to thanks; this ('what's in that?') is the natural one. Also: કંઈ નહીં (kain nahin).

yes.note: Politer: હા જી (haa ji) or just જી (ji).

excuse_me.note: Or simply ભાઈ (bhaai) to a man, બહેન (ben) to a woman.

good_morning.note: Formal; face to face people usually say નમસ્તે (namaste) or 'good morning'.

how_are_you.note: The everyday greeting is just કેમ છો? (kem chho?).

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also: તમને મળીને ખુશી થઈ (tamne maline khushi thai).

where_from.note: To a woman: તમે ક્યાંનાં છો? (tame kyaannaan chho?). Also: તમે ક્યાંથી આવો છો? (tame kyaanthi aavo chho?)

im_from.note: A woman says: હું …ની છું (hun …ni chhun). Also: હું …થી આવું છું (hun …thi aavun chhun).

speak_english.note: Also very natural: તમને અંગ્રેજી આવડે છે? (tamne angreji aavde chhe?)

dont_understand.note: About something just said: મને સમજ ના પડી (mane samaj naa padi).

speak_slowly.note: The polite question form -sho ('would you…?') with જરા (jaraa, 'a bit') does the work of 'please'.

what.note: Didn't catch it? શું કીધું? (shun kidhun?)

why.note: Also શા માટે? (shaa maate?). કેમ also means 'how', as in કેમ છો?

how_much.note: At a market, just આના કેટલા? (aanaa ketlaa?)

where_bathroom.note: ટૉઇલેટ (toilet) is also understood; signs may say શૌચાલય (shauchaalay).

what_means.note: Colloquial: આનો મતલબ શું? (aano matlab shun?)

bread.note: Thin wheat flatbread, the everyday bread. Loaf bread: બ્રેડ (bred).

menu_please.note: -jo makes it a polite request. Also: મેનુ આપશો? (menu aapsho?)

delicious.note: At someone's home: બહુ સરસ બન્યું છે! (bahu saras banyun chhe!)

no_meat.note: A woman says: હું માંસ ખાતી નથી (hun maans khaati nathi). Vegetarian: શાકાહારી (shaakaahaari).

enjoy_meal.note: No set phrase; hosts say this ('eat at leisure'). Also: પ્રેમથી જમજો (premthi jamjo).

straight_ahead.note: Giving directions: સીધા જાઓ (sidhaa jaao), 'go straight'.

stop_here.note: ઊભી agrees with ગાડી (gaadi, the vehicle). Also: અહીં ઉતારી દેજો (ahin utaari dejo).

hotel.note: In India it can also mean a restaurant or eatery.

want_to_go.note: No word for 'to' needed: મારે અમદાવાદ જવું છે (maare amdaavaad javun chhe).

pay_card.note: Literally 'will a card do?'. Also: કાર્ડથી પેમેન્ટ થશે? (kaardthi pement thashe?)

cash.note: The English કૅશ (kesh) is also widely used.

big.note: Agrees with the noun: મોટો (moto) masc., મોટી (moti) fem.; મોટું is neuter.

small.note: Agrees with the noun: નાનો (naano) masc., નાની (naani) fem.; નાનું is neuter.

tomorrow.note: In speech mostly just કાલે (kaale), which also means yesterday; the verb tense tells which.

yesterday.note: In speech mostly just કાલે (kaale), same as tomorrow; the past tense makes it clear.

now.note: Also હમણાં (hamnaan), which can also mean 'in a moment'.

good_evening.note: Formal; face to face people usually just say નમસ્તે (namaste).

good_night.note: Formal; people often say 'good night' in English, or આવજો (aavjo) when leaving.

im_lost.note: A woman says: હું રસ્તો ભૂલી ગઈ છું (hun rasto bhuli gai chhun).

pharmacy.note: In cities usually મેડિકલ સ્ટોર (medikal stor).

hospital.note: દવાખાનું (davaakhaanun) is a clinic or small hospital.

be_careful.note: As a sudden warning, like 'watch out!': સંભાળીને! (sambhaaline!)

i_like_it.note: About something just seen or tasted: મને ગમ્યું (mane gamyun).

dont_like_it.note: About something just seen or tasted: મને ન ગમ્યું (mane na gamyun).

im_tired.note: A woman says: હું થાકી ગઈ છું (hun thaaki gai chhun).

welcome.note: More respectful: પધારો! (padhaaro!). Formal or on signs: આપનું સ્વાગત છે (aapnun svaagat chhe).
